---
title: "Tickets"
description: "Lift a blocked tool call on the user's own words, answers, or rulings, and keep a record of it."
aliases: [grants.html]
---

A ticket records that one action, or every later action at one place, may go ahead.
A hook that blocks a tool call declares the tickets that lift its block and the
rules that mint one. Rules read the user's own words, their answers to the agent's
questions, and their cc-notes rulings, or a fact the hook's own condition proves.
No command mints a ticket. `capt-hook ticket` lists, shows, and revokes tickets that
rules minted, and records their uses.

## Declare the action that needs a ticket

Declare a `Tickets` instance, then attach it to a blocking tool hook with `tickets=`.
Its `action` function maps the event to a `Proposal`, which carries the values of the
declaration's place keys, every field that changes the action's effect as `payload`,
and a one-line `summary` for logs and messages.

For a messaging tool named `slack_reply` whose calls carry `channel`, `thread`,
`text`, and `broadcast`, save this hook as `.claude/hooks/slack_replies.py`:

```python
from captain_hook import (
    BaseHookEvent,
    Decide,
    Event,
    Names,
    Proposal,
    Reach,
    Rule,
    Tickets,
    Tool,
    UserAnswered,
    UserRuled,
    UserSaid,
    hook,
)
from captain_hook.tickets import Holds


def reply_action(evt: BaseHookEvent) -> Proposal:
    raw = evt.input.raw
    return Proposal(
        place={"channel": raw["channel"], "thread": raw["thread"]},
        payload={"text": raw["text"], "broadcast": raw.get("broadcast", False)},
        summary=f"reply in {raw['channel']}/{raw['thread']}",
    )


SLACK_REPLIES = Tickets(
    "slack.reply",
    ("channel", "thread"),
    Reach.ONCE,
    rules=(
        Rule("verbatim", UserSaid(Holds("text"))),
        Rule("answered", UserAnswered(Names())),
        Rule("ruled", UserRuled("channel")),
        Rule(
            "judged",
            Decide(
                "Allow only when the user's own words ask for a reply in this thread, "
                "or approve this text. Words about another thread permit nothing."
            ),
        ),
    ),
    deny="Ask the user to approve this reply, its thread, and its text.",
    action=reply_action,
    hook="slack_replies",
)

hook(
    Event.PreToolUse,
    "Replies need the user's permission.",
    only_if=[Tool("slack_reply")],
    block=True,
    tickets=SLACK_REPLIES,
)
```

The ticket check runs only after the hook matches and blocks. When a ticket covers
the call, the block lifts and the hook returns the context note
``<hook>: allowed by ticket `<id>` (<rule>).`` When none does, the agent gets the
declaration's `deny` sentence in place of the hook's own message. The user gets a
system message, `<hook>: <detail>`, saying what each rule found. Other hooks still
decide the event, and Claude Code's permission flow still applies.

`tickets=` requires `block=True`, a tool event, and a declaration with an `action`
function, and it rejects `max_fires`; registration raises `ValueError` otherwise.
The attachment fails closed. When the hook matches but its check does not finish
in time, the call blocks with "Retry the call; a ticket lifts this block only once
its check runs."

`Tickets` takes these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `kind` | The ticket kind this declaration finds and mints, such as `slack.reply` |
| `place` | The place keys every action and ticket carries |
| `reach` | `Reach.ONCE` or `Reach.PLACE`, for every ticket the declaration mints |
| `rules` | `Rule(name, when)` entries, tried in order |
| `deny` | The sentence the agent gets when no ticket covers the call |
| `action` | Maps the event to its `Proposal`; required for `tickets=` |
| `ttl` | How long a minted ticket lives; 7 days by default, `None` for no expiry |
| `window` | How many recent messages of each session the context reads; 60 by default |
| `machine` | Markers of a prompt a tool wrote for the user, which never counts as their words |
| `hook` | The hook name used in logs and the user's system message |

## Read a ticket record

A `Ticket` has these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `id` | Twelve hex characters, named in every allow |
| `kind` | The declaration that minted it |
| `tree` | The root session id of the session tree it was minted in |
| `place` | The exact value of each of the declaration's place keys |
| `reach` | `once` covers the action whose fingerprint it records; `place` covers every later action at its place |
| `rule` | The name of the rule that minted it |
| `evidence` | What that rule found |
| `fingerprint` | The digest of the action a once ticket covers; `None` for a place ticket |
| `author` | `hook:<hook>@<session>/<agent>` for a ticket a hook minted |
| `created`, `expires`, `revoked` | When it was minted, when it stops covering anything, and when it was revoked |

Each evidence item has an `id` the judge cites, such as `words:1a2b3c4d5e6f` or
`ask:toolu_01#0`. Its `source` names where it came from: `prompt`, `queued`, `plan`,
`ask`, `board`, `ccn`, `touch`, or a hook's own. `quote` holds the words themselves,
`said_at` the time when the source records one, and `detail` the context read beside
the quote, such as the agent message it answers.

A ticket has no use budget. The hook that finds or mints it records no use; a
downstream system that enforces the action records one per call with
[`capt-hook ticket spend`](#manage-tickets-from-the-cli).

## Choose the place and the reach {#choose-the-place-and-reach}

The place keys name where an action lands, and each ticket holds one exact value
per key, with no patterns or wildcards. A proposal must carry exactly the declaration's
place keys. Any other set raises `ValueError`, which the check turns into a deny.
An empty value is a value, so a top-level post with `thread=""` gets its own tickets.

`Reach.ONCE` binds a minted ticket to the action's fingerprint, a digest of the
place and the payload, so it covers the same action again and nothing else. Put
every effect-bearing field in `payload`, or a once ticket covers actions that differ
in it. `Reach.PLACE` leaves the fingerprint out, so the ticket covers every later
action at its place, whatever the payload.

A ticket belongs to the session tree it was minted in, which is the root session and
every subagent it spawns. An attended Claude session in the terminal of a live Orca
dispatch joins the tree of its Run's coordinator, the Claude session in the terminal
Orca names as the Run's `coordinator_handle`. Like a subagent, it reads that session as
its root. The coordinator's prompts and answers are the user's, the lane's own prompts
are its brief, and the tickets the lane mints belong to the coordinator's tree. No other
tree sees them.

A ticket stops covering anything when it expires or is revoked. Pick `ttl` for how
long the permission should last. A once ticket with a short `ttl` covers an
identical retry, and a place ticket with a long one covers a standing permission.

## Write rules from conditions

`Rule(name, when)` mints a ticket when its condition holds. `decide` tries the rules
in order, and the first that holds mints the ticket with the evidence the condition
found. The name lands on the ticket as `rule` and in each deny's detail.

Import these conditions from `captain_hook`:

| Condition | Holds when | Evidence |
|-----------|------------|----------|
| `UserSaid(*patterns)` | The user's words across the session tree match any pattern; with none, any words | The matching words |
| `UserAnswered(*patterns, approved=True)` | An answer's question and options match any pattern; with `approved`, only approving answers count | The matching answers |
| `UserRuled(key, ids=(), tags=frozenset())` | A cc-notes ruling names the action's `key` value whole and carries every tag, or a ruling in `ids` stands | The rulings |
| `Touched(*patterns)` | An earlier tool call in the tree matches, by its input or result; with no patterns, it names the place | The calls |
| `Decide(rules, ...)` | The judge allows, citing evidence | The cited items |

A pattern is a regex string, a `Clause`, or a `Matcher`. `Names(*keys)` matches text
that names every non-empty place value of `keys` as a whole name, every place key
when none are given; `Names()` matches neither `C0123` inside `C01234` nor
`com.x` inside `com.x.helper`. `Holds(key)` matches text that holds the payload
field `key` verbatim, whitespace folded, as whole words.

`UserAnswered` reads `AskUserQuestion` answers and cc-present board picks, typed
inputs, feedback, and decisions. An approving answer picks an option other than the
last one shown, or types words with no hold, such as `no`, `wait`, `not yet`, or
`cancel`.

`UserRuled` reads only cc-notes answers last written before the acting session
started, so an agent cannot record a ruling and act on it in the same session.
With `key`, it searches answers whose body names that place value. With `ids`, it
reads those answers by id, whatever action they cover.

`And`, `Or`, and `Not` compose these like any other condition. `And` holds when
every part holds and gathers every part's evidence; `Or` takes the first part that
holds; `Not` holds with no evidence. A plain condition such as `Tool` holds in a
rule too, and contributes no evidence.

Inside a rule, `UserSaid` ignores its `scope`.

A condition of your own subclasses `CustomTicketCondition` and implements
`evidence(ctx)`, returning a list of `Evidence` or `None` when it does not hold.
`Holds`, `Matcher`, `CustomTicketCondition`, and `Evidence` come from
`captain_hook.tickets`.

## Let the judge decide {#let-the-judge-decide}

`Decide(rules)` reads the evidence of the conditions in `over`. By default that is
every word of the user's, through `UserSaid()`, and every answer, through
`UserAnswered(approved=False)`. It asks whether one item permits exactly this action under the `rules` prose. With
no evidence it finds nothing and calls no model.

TypeSafe Jev answers first, picking the one item that permits the action. When it
puts 0.8 or more on one item, the action goes ahead on that citation with no LLM
call. Any other answer, or a Jev failure, goes to the LLM, which returns a `Verdict`
with `allow`, `reason`, `relied_on`, and `refusal`. An allow counts only for the
items it cites in `relied_on`; an allow that cites none, and a refusal, find
nothing. With `llm=False`, Jev alone judges, and an answer it does not settle finds
nothing.

A judge that gives no verdict within `deadline`, 20 seconds capped by the time left
in the request, or whose backend fails raises `Undecided`. The declaration reports
that rule as `<rule>: the judge gave no verdict (...)` and tries the next one, so
a judge failure never lets an action through.

Narrow `over` to read less. The general pack's owner-named lifts pass
`over=(UserSaid(Names(key)), UserAnswered(Names(key), approved=False))`, so the
judge reads only words and answers that name the target. `model` defaults to
`"small"`; `contexts`, `transcript`, `root_transcript`, and `tool_results` add what
`llm_evaluate` reads.

## Know what counts as the user's words

`Context` holds the action and what the session tree knows about what the user wants.
`Tickets.context(evt, action)` builds the live one; conditions read it.

| Attribute | Holds |
|-----------|-------|
| `kind`, `action` | The declaration's kind and the `Proposal` to cover; `place` is the action's place |
| `tree`, `trees` | The acting tree's root session id, and every tree whose tickets cover the action |
| `session`, `agent`, `call` | The acting session, the acting agent or `main`, and the pending call id |
| `said` | The user's words, oldest first |
| `answers` | `Answer` items with `question`, `options`, `chosen`, and `typed` |
| `touches` | The tree's tool calls with their input and result |
| `rulings(term, tags)`, `ruling(id)` | cc-notes rulings written before the session started |
| `fact(Type, default)` | A lookup the hook injects, built once per context |

Only the user's own words count as `said`. Those are the root session's prompts,
messages the user queued while the agent worked, and what they typed when rejecting a plan in the
root session. A lane's own prompts are its brief and its teammates' messages, never
the user's. Teammate messages, tool output, notifications, channel lines, harness
envelopes, and prompts carrying a `machine` marker never count. Each prompt carries
the end of the agent message it answers in its `detail`.

The sources read the last `window` messages of each session. A lane also reads the
root session's earlier mentions of the place values, however far back they sit.
`said`, `answers`, and `touches` are read once per context, on first use.

`ctx.fact(Type, default)` returns the value of type `Type` a hook injected, or builds
it with `default(ctx)` and keeps it, such as a thread a condition reads from a chat
system.

## Follow the check order

`Tickets.decide(ctx)` stops at the first allow:

1. Find the newest live ticket of this kind in the context's trees that covers the
   action, with the same place and, for a once ticket, the same fingerprint. It
   allows with no rule run.
2. Otherwise, try each rule in order. The first whose condition finds evidence mints
   a ticket with the declaration's reach and `ttl` and allows.
3. A rule whose judge raises `Undecided` finds nothing, and the next rule runs.
4. When no rule holds, deny with `deny` as the message and a detail such as
   `verbatim: nothing found; answered: nothing found`.

`Tickets.check(evt, action=None)` builds the context and runs `decide`, failing
closed. A store, source, or judge error denies with the detail
`The ticket check failed (<error>).`

A hook that lets the action through when its own check cannot finish, after an
exception or a lookup that times out, calls `Tickets.unchecked(ctx, cause)`. It
mints a once ticket at the action's place with rule `unchecked`, one evidence item
from source `hook` quoting the cause, and a ten-minute lifetime, so the record says
why nothing checked the action. Its fingerprint binds it to this action, so it
covers no later one.

Pass a `Proposal` to check an action other
than the one `action` maps the event to, such as each of several calls in one
event; a declaration used only this way may omit `action`.

`check` and `decide` return a truthy `Allow(ticket, minted)` or a falsy
`Deny(message, detail)`. `Allow.reason` reads `ticket <id> minted by rule <name>`,
or `found for rule <name>` for a ticket that already covered the action.

## Manage tickets from the CLI

| Command | Does |
|---------|------|
| `capt-hook ticket list [--kind K] [--tree T] [--all]` | Lists live tickets; `--all` adds expired and revoked ones |
| `capt-hook ticket show <id>` | Prints the record as JSON and every use recorded against it |
| `capt-hook ticket revoke <id>` | Revokes the ticket; it covers nothing from then on |
| `capt-hook ticket spend <id> ...` | Records a use for a downstream system |
| `capt-hook ticket release <id> --call <call>` | Hands back the use recorded for a call that never took effect |

Tickets live in `~/.claude/state/hooks/tickets.db`, one SQLite file every session on
the machine reads. `CAPTAIN_HOOK_STATE_DIR` moves the state directory and the file
with it.

A system that enforces the action itself, such as the cc-slack daemon, records each
use with `spend`. Replace the uppercase placeholders:

```bash
uvx capt-hook ticket spend TICKET_ID \
  --place channel=C0123 --place thread=1712345678.000100 \
  --tree ROOT_SESSION_ID --session SESSION_ID --agent main \
  --call CALL_ID --fingerprint ACTION_FINGERPRINT \
  --summary 'reply in C0123/1712345678.000100'
```

Repeat `--place` for every place key. Every option is required except `--agent`,
which defaults to `main`. `--fingerprint` is the action's `Proposal.fingerprint`;
a once ticket covers only its own. `spend` prints `{"ticket": ...}` and records one
use per call, so a repeat for the same call adds nothing. It exits non-zero with the
reason when the ticket does not exist, has expired or been revoked, belongs to
another tree, or covers another place or action.

Run `release` only when the action did not happen, such as a write the
remote system refused. It prints the ticket and the number of uses released.

## Test tickets

Unit-test a declaration's rules with `Context.fake`, which takes the action and its
sources outright as `said`, `answers`, `touches`, `rulings`, and `facts`. A plain
string in `said` is one of the user's prompts. `decide` mints into the real store, so point
`CAPTAIN_HOOK_STATE_DIR` at a temporary directory:

```python
from captain_hook import Context
from captain_hook.tickets import Allow

from slack_replies import SLACK_REPLIES


def test_a_verbatim_request_mints_a_once_ticket(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    monkeypatch.setenv("CAPTAIN_HOOK_STATE_DIR", str(tmp_path))
    ctx = Context.fake(
        "slack.reply",
        {"channel": "C0123", "thread": "1712345678.000100"},
        payload={"text": "Deploy finished.", "broadcast": False},
        said=['Reply "Deploy finished." in that thread.'],
    )
    first = SLACK_REPLIES.decide(ctx)
    assert isinstance(first, Allow) and first.minted and first.ticket.rule == "verbatim"
    again = SLACK_REPLIES.decide(ctx)
    assert isinstance(again, Allow) and not again.minted and again.ticket.id == first.ticket.id
```

A fake context has no event. `Decide` and plain conditions such as `Tool` read the
event, so a fake context that reaches one raises `TypeError`; cover those rules in
the hook's inline tests. A fake context's rulings match by name and ignore `tags`.

Inline tests seed the store with `Input(tickets=[...])`. Each test starts from an
empty store holding only its seeds. Match the input's `session_id` to the ticket's
`tree`, and stub `ccn` and `cc-present` so the rules read no real records. In
`slack_replies.py`, give the `hook(...)` call its tests:

```python
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from captain_hook import Block, Input, Reach, Ticket, Warn

SEEDED = Ticket(
    id="0123456789ab",
    kind="slack.reply",
    tree="example-root",
    place={"channel": "C0123", "thread": "1712345678.000100"},
    reach=Reach.PLACE,
    rule="seed",
    author="test",
    created=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC),
)
STUBS = {"ccn answer search": "[]", "cc-present outcomes": "{}"}


def reply(thread: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"channel": "C0123", "thread": thread, "text": "Deploy finished."}


hook(
    Event.PreToolUse,
    "Replies need the user's permission.",
    only_if=[Tool("slack_reply")],
    block=True,
    tickets=SLACK_REPLIES,
    tests={
        Input(
            tool="slack_reply", tool_input=reply("1712345678.000100"),
            session_id="example-root", tickets=[SEEDED], commands=STUBS,
        ): Warn(pattern="allowed by ticket `0123456789ab`"),
        Input(
            tool="slack_reply", tool_input=reply("1712345678.000200"),
            session_id="example-root", tickets=[SEEDED], commands=STUBS,
        ): Block(pattern="Ask the user to approve this reply"),
    },
)
```

A lifted block returns a context note, so its inline expectation is `Warn`.

## Lift a session guard block {#lift-a-session-guard-block}

The `general` pack's session guards block a terminal close, a launchd service stop,
a lane's `TaskStop`, and a `kill`, and lift each through these ticket kinds:

| Kind | Place | Reach, lifetime | Rules, in order |
|------|-------|-----------------|-----------------|
| `sessions.close` | `terminal` | once, 2 minutes | `ruling`, a cc-notes answer naming the handle; `created-here`, this session created the terminal |
| `sessions.close-settled` | none | place, no expiry | `class-ruling`, the judge reads standing rulings `c9b27c1` and `6190a4a` |
| `sessions.close.owner` | `terminal` | once, 1 hour | `user-named`, the judge reads the user's words and answers naming the handle |
| `sessions.launchctl` | `service` | once, 2 minutes | `ruling`, a cc-notes answer naming the service label |
| `sessions.launchctl.owner` | `service` | once, 1 hour | `user-named`, the judge reads the user's words and answers naming the label |
| `sessions.task-stop` | `agent`, `task` | place, 7 days | `spawned-here`, then `ruling`; minted on spawn as `teammate` or `shell` |
| `sessions.kill` | `program`, `process` | once, 2 minutes | `ruling`, an answer tagged `scope:durable` and `sessions-guard` naming the program |
| `sessions.kill-session` | `program`, `process` | once, 2 minutes | `ruling`, the judge reads answers tagged `scope:durable` and `sessions-guard` naming the program, and allows a codex session hosting no other session only when the words list its pid or set an age floor it clears |

A ruling covers its target while it stands. Every check reads it again, so each new
call on that target mints its own once ticket, and the ticket's two minutes cover
an identical retry without reading the rules. A ruling counts only when its body
names the value as a whole name and it was last written before the acting session
started; editing it during the session takes it out of that session.

The terminal close tries `sessions.close`, then `sessions.close-settled`, then the
owner-named lift. `created-here` holds when this session's transcript records
creating the terminal, through a lone, bare `orca terminal create` call or an
`orca-launch.sh` call whose receipt names it, no Orca dispatch names the terminal,
and its agent idles at a prompt with no pending question.

`sessions.close-settled` applies only to the root session coordinating the Run
whose dispatch holds the terminal, when Orca records that dispatch as `completed`
or `failed` and its agent idles. The judge decides whether the standing rulings
cover the terminal's Orca record. Its first allow mints a place ticket with no
expiry, so later settled closes in that tree skip the judge; the guard still checks
the dispatch, the idle prompt, and the caller before each close. After the lift, it
reads the dispatch and the screen again. If either changed, it blocks the close
and tells the user
`sessions: the terminal's dispatch or idle prompt changed while the judge decided.`

The `.owner` kinds serve only the spawning root: the main thread of a session with
no root session above it. They run after the other lifts deny, and their judge reads only the
user's words and answers that name the exact handle or label. A description, a
general cleanup request, or words naming another target permit nothing.

`sessions.task-stop` covers one task for the agent that started it. On
`PostToolUse`, the pack mints a ticket at place `{agent: "<session>/<agent>", task}`
for a teammate an `Agent` or `Task` call spawned and for a background task a `Bash`
or `Monitor` call started, so the ticket outlives compaction. `spawned-here` holds
when the agent's own transcript records spawning a `<name>@session-<8 hex>`
teammate, or a `Bash` or `Monitor` call whose result names the background task id,
so an agent stops its own background shell even when no ticket was minted. The root
session's `TaskStop` is never guarded.

`sessions.kill` names the process as `<pid>@<start time>`, so a ticket never covers
a recycled pid. The program is the script for a `python`, `node`, `bun`, `deno`,
`ruby`, or `perl` process, such as `desk-runner.py`, and the executable otherwise.

A lifted terminal close or `launchctl` command must run once. It comes first at top
level, at the start of the Bash payload, with only pipe successors. Loops, `&&` or `;`
chains, background calls, wrappers, substitutions, and respelled variables keep
the block. The `launchctl` payload carries its verb, so a ticket for `kickstart`
does not cover `bootout` of the same service.
